mainTopic: The opinion of רבי אליעזר that preparations for מילה (such as carrying the knife) override שבת, רבי עקיבא's opposing rule, and the גמרא's question about why רבי אליעזר requires the knife to be carried uncovered.
overview: The new פרק opens with a משנה about מילה on שבת. רבי אליעזר holds that even the preparations for מילה override שבת: the knife may be carried on שבת uncovered, and one may even cut wood to forge a new knife. רבי עקיבא disagrees: only the מילה itself overrides שבת, because the preparations could have been done before שבת. The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר wants the knife uncovered, and concludes that it is out of love for the מצוה (חבובי מצוה). It then asks how many עדים are needed when the knife is covered in a time of danger, and this question is not resolved. A ברייתא reports that רבי אליעזר's town followed his ruling and רבי יוסי הגלילי's town ate poultry in milk. The story of לוי shows that one may not punish a town for following its own רב. Aggadot follow in praise of מילה: a city that followed רבי אליעזר was rewarded, and מצוות accepted with joy or defended with self-sacrifice remain strong, unlike תפילין. The story of אלישע בעל כנפים illustrates that point. The amud ends by beginning a story about a forgotten knife for a ברית on שבת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Carry the מילה knife uncovered on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that if the מילה knife was not brought before שבת, it may be carried on שבת openly. In a time of danger, it is carried covered in front of witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: If he did not bring the knife before שבת, he brings it on שבת uncovered. In a time of danger, he covers it in front of witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the new פרק with רבי אליעזר's ruling that one may carry the מילה knife on שבת, and that it should be carried in the open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying in a public area is normally forbidden on שבת. רבי אליעזר holds that this preparation for מילה (an מכשיר מצוה) overrides שבת just like the מילה itself. He adds two details: the knife goes uncovered in normal times, and covered with witnesses when the government forbids מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Danger, here a time of government persecution against מילה

steps.confusionAlert: The 'danger' here is not danger to the baby. It refers to times when non-Jewish rulers banned מילה, so carrying the knife openly could get a person killed.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא הֵבִיא כְּלִי מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: If he did not bring the implement on Shabbat eve,
phrases.notes: The implement is the circumcision knife.

phrases.english: he brings it on Shabbat uncovered,
and in a time of danger he covers it, in the presence of witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אִם לֹא הֵבִיא כְּלִי מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, carrying the מילה knife on שבת is permitted. It should be carried uncovered, or covered in front of witnesses in a time of danger.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Even making the knife from scratch is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר goes further: one may cut trees to make charcoal in order to forge an iron knife for the מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר also said: One may cut down trees to make charcoal, in order to make an iron tool.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a more extreme statement from רבי אליעזר: even the earliest preparations for the מילה override שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying is one small preparation. Here רבי אליעזר allows a whole chain of מלאכות: cutting wood, burning charcoal, and forging iron. This shows that in his view every preparation needed for the מילה overrides שבת, no matter how far removed it is.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, introducing an additional ruling

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said:
One may cut down trees to make charcoal
in order to make an iron (implement).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי אליעזר's view from carrying the knife to making the knife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, all preparations for מילה override שבת, even making the iron knife from raw materials.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's rule: Only what could not be done before שבת overrides it
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא states a general rule. Any מלאכה that could have been done before שבת does not override שבת. The מילה itself, which cannot be done before שבת, does override it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא stated a rule: Any מלאכה that could be done before שבת does not override שבת. But מילה, which cannot be done before שבת, does override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי עקיבא, who disagrees with רבי אליעזר and limits what is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's test is simple: could this have been done on Friday? Carrying or making the knife could have been done earlier, so it is forbidden on שבת. The מילה must happen on the eighth day, which may fall on שבת, so only the מילה itself overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden creative act on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that the preparations for מילה (מכשירי מילה) override שבת. רבי עקיבא holds that only the מילה itself overrides שבת, because the preparations could have been done before שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי עקיבא's rule is the accepted הלכה. Anyone who did not bring the knife before שבת may not carry it through a public area on שבת.

phrases.english: A principle was stated by Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: Any prohibited labor that can be done on Shabbat eve
does not override Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִילָה שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: and circumcision, which cannot be done on Shabbat eve,
overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אליעזר's broad permission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only what could not have been done before שבת overrides שבת. The מילה itself overrides שבת, but its preparations do not.

steps.title: Why must the knife be uncovered: love of the מצוה or avoiding suspicion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אליעזר's requirement to carry the knife uncovered. Is it to show love for the מצוה, or to avoid people suspecting him of breaking שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is רבי אליעזר's reason because of love for the מצוה, or perhaps because of suspicion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the reason behind רבי אליעזר's ruling that the knife is carried uncovered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible reasons. The first is חבובי מצוה: carrying the knife openly shows love for and pride in the מצוה. The second is חשדא: if the knife is hidden, onlookers may think he is carrying something ordinary and breaking שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them, an open question
Love for the מצוה, showing it is dear to us
Suspicion, that people may think he is sinning

phrases.english: GEMARA: A dilemma was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִשּׁוּם חַבּוֹבֵי מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: Is Rabbi Eliezer's reason due to affection for the מצוה,
or perhaps due to suspicion?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason for רבי אליעזר's requirement that the knife be carried uncovered.

steps.title: What practical difference does the reason make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it makes in practice which reason is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. Before trying to settle the question, the גמרא asks for a case where the two reasons would lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a question to have real-world consequences. If both reasons always led to the same ruling, it would not matter which one is true.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference results from this?

phrases.english: What practical difference is there?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two possible reasons lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: carrying it covered in front of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The difference is carrying the knife covered with witnesses present. If the reason is love of the מצוה, it must be uncovered. If the reason is suspicion, covered with witnesses is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is bringing it covered in front of witnesses. If you say the reason is love of the מצוה, then uncovered is allowed and covered is not. But if you say the reason is suspicion, even covered is fine, because the witnesses know what it is for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the previous question by naming the case where the two reasons split: a covered knife carried with witnesses present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses remove any suspicion, because they know the knife is for a מילה. So under חשדא, covering is fine. Under חבובי מצוה, the point is to show the מצוה publicly, and witnesses do not achieve that, so the knife must stay uncovered.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring. Here it is meant literally: bringing (carrying) the knife

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with the משנה's 'danger' case. There, covering with witnesses is allowed only because of danger. Here the question is about normal times.

phrases.english: To bring it covered in the presence of witnesses.
If you say it is due to affection for the מצוה,
uncovered, yes; covered, no.
But if you say it is due to suspicion,
even covered is perfectly fine.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two reasons differ about carrying the knife covered with witnesses present in normal times. Under חבובי מצוה it is forbidden, and under חשדא it is permitted.

steps.title: Restating the dilemma: What is the law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the question by asking: so which reason is correct?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא formally restates its question and sets up the attempts to resolve it, which come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the practical difference is clear, the גמרא asks directly which reason is right. The next step answers this question.

phrases.english: What is the resolution?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר's reason is חבובי מצוה or חשדא, which decides whether a covered knife carried with witnesses is allowed.

steps.title: רבי לוי: It is about love for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי answers the open question. רבי אליעזר required the knife to be uncovered only to show love for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי לוי said: רבי אליעזר only said this ruling to show love for the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the question it asked in Step 7. רבי לוי says the reason is love of the מצוה, not fear of suspicion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that the two reasons give different results when the knife is carried covered with עדים present. By choosing 'love of the מצוה', רבי לוי's view means the knife must be uncovered even when עדים are there.

keyTerms.meaning: To show love and fondness for the מצוה
He only said it because of

phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Levi said:
Rabbi Eliezer did not say it
except to show love for the מצוה.
phrases.notes: Carrying the knife openly in the street shows pride in the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question 'so which reason is correct?' from Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reason stands behind carrying the knife uncovered?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is for חבובי מצוה, love of the מצוה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי לוי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the knife is brought uncovered and never covered. This supports the 'love of the מצוה' reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: One brings it uncovered, and one does not bring it covered. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רבי לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא flatly says 'not covered', with no exception for when עדים are present. If the only worry were suspicion, carrying it covered with עדים would be allowed. A total ban fits the 'love of the מצוה' reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (introduces support)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
He brings it uncovered
and he does not bring it covered,
phrases.notes: No exception is mentioned for when witnesses are present.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives support from a ברייתא to רבי לוי's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רבי לוי's claim that the reason is חבובי מצוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that bans carrying the knife covered with no exception

steps.title: רב אשי: The משנה's wording proves it too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the משנה closely. Covering with עדים is allowed only in danger, so outside of danger it must be uncovered even with עדים. That shows the reason is love of the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Our משנה is also precise this way, because it teaches: 'And in a time of danger he covers it in front of עדים.' In danger, yes. Not in danger, no. Learn from this that the reason is love of the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a second proof, this time from the exact wording of our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows 'covered with עדים' only in a time of danger. If the reason were suspicion, covering with עדים would work at any time, and the משנה would not need to limit it to danger. Since it does limit it, the reason must be love of the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה's wording is also precise (supports this)
In a time of danger (e.g., when the government forbids מילה)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Our Mishnah is also precise this way,
since it teaches: And in a time of danger
he covers it in front of witnesses,
in danger, yes,
not in danger, no,
phrases.notes: Even with witnesses, it may not be covered.

phrases.english: learn from this that it is because of love for the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof, from the משנה's own wording.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A close reading of the משנה: covering with עדים is allowed only in danger

steps.title: The גמרא accepts the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: the reason is love of the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This short line settles the matter. The knife is carried uncovered out of love for the מצוה, so outside of danger it must be uncovered even if עדים are present.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's rule of carrying the knife uncovered is because of חבובי מצוה. So in normal times it must be uncovered even with עדים. Only in a time of danger may it be covered with עדים.

phrases.english: Learn from this (it is indeed so).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof of Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reason is חבובי מצוה, and covering with עדים is allowed only in danger.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: the custom in times of danger
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא repeats רבי אליעזר's rule. It adds רבי יהודה's report that in times of danger people carried the knife covered in front of עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: He brings it uncovered and does not bring it covered. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אליעזר: In a time of danger, the custom was to bring it covered in front of עדים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא about the time-of-danger custom. This sets up the next question about the עדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא matches the משנה: uncovered normally, covered with עדים only in danger. Its new detail is that this was a known custom. Its mention of 'עדים' leads straight into the question of how many are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was the custom; people used to do this

steps.confusionAlert: 'Danger' here does not mean danger to the baby. It means a time when the government made decrees against מילה, so carrying the knife openly could get a person caught.

phrases.english: Another baraita taught:
He brings it uncovered and does not bring it covered,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
It was the custom in a time of danger

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ מְבִיאִין מְכוּסֶּה עַל פִּי עֵדִים.
phrases.english: that they would bring it covered in front of witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for the rule to the details of the time-of-danger exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In times of danger, the custom was to carry the knife covered in front of עדים.

steps.title: How many witnesses are needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'עדים' means the carrier plus one more person, or the carrier plus two more people.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: The 'עדים' it mentions: is it the carrier and one other person, or perhaps the carrier and two others?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question about the exact meaning of 'עדים' in the danger case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the carrier himself counts toward the pair of עדים. If he does, only one more person is needed. If not, two more people are needed besides him.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked; a question that was raised (a real unknown)

phrases.english: They asked:
the witnesses that it mentions:
is it he and one other,
or perhaps he and two others?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of 'עדים' mentioned in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the carrier count as one of the עדים, or are two other people needed?

steps.title: Attempted proof from the plural word 'witnesses'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the משנה's plural word 'עדים' that two people are needed besides the carrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And in danger he covers it in front of עדים.' If you say it means the carrier and two others, that fits well. But if you say it means the carrier and one other, why does it say 'עדים' (plural)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a proof that the carrier plus two others are needed, based on the plural form of the word 'עדים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'עדים' in the plural, meaning more than one witness. If only one person besides the carrier were needed, the משנה should have said 'עד' (one witness). So it seems two others are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say this, it makes sense

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And in danger he covers it in front of witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא הוּא וּתְרֵי — שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: If you say it is he and two others, that fits well,
but if you say it is he and one other,
why does it say 'witnesses'?
phrases.notes: There would be only one witness besides the carrier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of Step 13 from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That the carrier plus two others are needed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plural word 'עדים' in the משנה

steps.title: Rejection: they are called witnesses because they could testify elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The carrier and one other can still be called 'עדים' because both are fit to be witnesses in other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are called 'עדים' because they are fit to testify in another place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'עדים' can describe the carrier and the one other person together. Each of them is a kosher witness in general, so as a pair they can be called 'עדים'. The plural word therefore does not prove that two others are needed, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to testify; qualified as witnesses
In another place; in other cases

phrases.english: Because they are fit to testify elsewhere.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the plural word in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the plural 'עדים' for the 'carrier plus two others' view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plural can include the carrier and one other, since both are generally fit to testify.

steps.title: In רבי אליעזר's town they cut wood on שבת to forge a מילה knife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line 'ועוד אמר רבי אליעזר' and brings a ברייתא: in רבי אליעזר's town people cut trees on שבת to make charcoal for forging iron for מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And furthermore, רבי אליעזר said' (that one may even cut wood to make charcoal for the מילה). The Rabbis taught in a ברייתא: In רבי אליעזר's place, people would cut down trees to make charcoal, in order to forge iron, on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It brings a ברייתא showing that people in רבי אליעזר's town really followed his lenient ruling in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that even the steps that prepare for מילה override שבת. That includes cutting trees, making charcoal, and forging a knife. The ברייתא shows this was not only theory: his town actually lived by it.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place, meaning the town where a רב ruled and people followed him
Iron, here the metal knife used for מילה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the theme of the whole section: in a רב's own town, people may follow his ruling even when others disagree.

phrases.english: "And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said"
phrases.notes: Quoting the next line of the משנה, which allows cutting wood for charcoal for the מילה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught (in a baraita):
In the place of Rabbi Eliezer
they would cut down trees
to make charcoal
to forge iron (for the circumcision knife) on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Every step of preparation was done on שבת itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of carrying the knife in front of עדים to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי אליעזר's town, people cut wood on שבת to make charcoal and forge a knife for מילה, following his ruling.

steps.title: In רבי יוסי הגלילי's town they ate poultry in milk
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא adds a parallel case: in רבי יוסי הגלילי's town, people ate poultry cooked in milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: In רבי יוסי הגלילי's place, people would eat chicken (poultry) meat in milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second example of a town that followed its own רב. In רבי יוסי הגלילי's town, people ate poultry with milk because he held it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most חכמים forbid poultry in milk, at least מדרבנן. רבי יוסי הגלילי held that בשר בחלב does not apply to birds at all. His town followed his ruling. This is the same pattern as רבי אליעזר's town.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the הלכה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. It only reports what was done in his town, where people followed his ruling.

phrases.english: In the place of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili
they would eat poultry meat in milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel example in the same ברייתא of a town following its local רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יוסי הגלילי's town, people ate poultry in milk, following his view.

steps.title: לוי is served a peacock head in milk and does not eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells a story: לוי visited the house of יוסף the hunter, was served a peacock head in milk, and did not eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי happened to come to the house of יוסף the hunter. They served him a peacock's head in milk. He did not eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to poultry in milk. It is setting up the next move, where רבי asks לוי a question about what happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A peacock is a bird, so this is exactly the case of poultry in milk. לוי himself held it is forbidden, so he did not eat. But he also did nothing against his hosts.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought before him, they served him

phrases.english: Levi happened to come to the house of Yosef the hunter.
They served him the head of a peacock in milk,
he did not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life story showing how a town that ate poultry in milk was treated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי refused to eat poultry in milk, but he did not act against his hosts.

steps.title: רבי asks לוי why he did not excommunicate them
steps.stepSummary: When לוי came before רבי, רבי challenged him: why did you not put those people in נידוי?
steps.simpleTranslation: When לוי came before רבי, רבי said to him: Why did you not excommunicate them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי challenges לוי for not punishing people who ate poultry in milk. This question sets up לוי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי assumes poultry in milk is forbidden, so the hosts were openly breaking a rule of the חכמים. In his view, a learned visitor like לוי should have placed them in שמתא (נידוי).

keyTerms.meaning: You excommunicate them (from שמתא, a ban)

phrases.english: When he (Levi) came before Rabbi,
he said to him: Why did you not excommunicate them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges לוי's choice to stay silent in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's failure to punish the hosts who served poultry in milk
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Poultry in milk is forbidden, so people who openly eat it should be placed in נידוי.

steps.title: לוי answers that it was רבי יהודה בן בתירה's town
steps.stepSummary: לוי explains that the place was under רבי יהודה בן בתירה, who may have taught them like רבי יוסי הגלילי. So they were following their own רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said to him: It was the place of רבי יהודה בן בתירה. I said to myself: Perhaps he taught them like רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי defends himself. Since the local רב may have ruled leniently, the townspeople were not sinners, and he could not punish them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a town follows its own רב's ruling, an outside scholar may not ban them, even if he disagrees. The possibility alone that רבי יהודה בן בתירה ruled like רבי יוסי הגלילי was enough for לוי to hold back.

keyTerms.meaning: His place, his area of authority
He taught them, he expounded for them

steps.whatToRemember: A town may follow its own רב (מרא דאתרא). An outside scholar who disagrees may not punish them for following his ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the whole section: רבי אליעזר's town and רבי יוסי הגלילי's town acted properly by following their own רבנים.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה הֲוָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: It was the place of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
and I said (to myself): Perhaps he taught them
in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Local authority: the people may have been following their own רב's lenient ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone eating poultry in milk is breaking the rule and deserves נידוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a place where the local רב may permit it, the people are not punished.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי's source from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה where רבי יוסי הגלילי derives from the פסוק that birds are not included in בשר בחלב, because they have no 'mother's milk'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: It says 'Do not eat any נבלה,' and it says 'Do not cook a kid in its mother's milk.' Whatever is forbidden as נבלה is forbidden to cook in milk. A bird is forbidden as נבלה, so I might think it is forbidden to cook in milk. That is why the פסוק says 'in its mother's milk': this excludes a bird, which has no mother's milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבי יוסי הגלילי's view comes from. It quotes his reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both phrases appear in the same פסוק, so he first links them: anything that can be נבלה is included in בשר בחלב. That would include birds. But the words 'its mother's milk' limit the rule to animals that nurse their young, and birds do not.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
It is stated: "You shall not eat anything that dies of itself (any neveilah),"
and it is stated: "You shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk."
phrases.notes: Both phrases are in the same פסוק (דברים יד:כא), so they are linked.

phrases.english: That which is forbidden because of neveilah —
it is forbidden to cook it in milk.
Poultry, which is forbidden because of neveilah,
I might think it should be forbidden to cook in milk —
therefore the verse says: "in its mother's milk,"

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא עוֹף שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חֲלֵב אֵם.
phrases.english: which excludes poultry, which has no mother's milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי that לוי mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that poultry in milk is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה reading the words 'בחלב אמו' in דברים יד:כא

steps.title: A city that followed רבי אליעזר lived out full lives
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reports that a city in ארץ ישראל followed רבי אליעזר's ruling on מילה, and its people died only at their proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: There was one city in ארץ ישראל where they acted like רבי אליעזר, and they would die at their proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי אליעזר. רבי יצחק describes the reward of a city that followed his ruling about preparing for מילה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי אליעזר meant doing even the preparations for מילה on שבת. Even so, the city was not punished as if it had broken שבת. Instead it was rewarded with full lives, because of its love for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: They acted according to רבי אליעזר
Dying at their proper time, not young

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
There was one city in Eretz Yisrael
where they would act in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer
and they would die at their appointed time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: עִיר אַחַת הָיְתָה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי אליעזר's town from step 16, after the side discussion about poultry in milk.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A city that followed רבי אליעזר on מילה was rewarded with full lives.

steps.title: That city was spared the Roman decree against circumcision
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק adds that when the wicked kingdom banned מילה for all of Israel, that city was left out of the decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not only that, but once the wicked kingdom made a decree against Israel forbidding מילה, and against that city it did not make the decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds a second, bigger reward. The city that honored מילה was protected from the Roman ban on מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward matches the מצוה exactly. The city went to great lengths for מילה, so it was allowed to keep doing מילה when everyone else was forbidden. This closes the section on רבי אליעזר's view with praise for the city's devotion.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only that, but even more

steps.whatToRemember: A town may follow its own רב: רבי אליעזר's town did preparations for מילה on שבת, and רבי יוסי הגלילי's town ate poultry in milk. A city that followed רבי אליעזר out of love for מילה was rewarded with long life and was spared the decree against מילה.

phrases.english: And not only that, but on one occasion
the wicked kingdom issued
a decree against the Jewish people concerning circumcision,
but against that city it did not issue the decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יצחק's statement with an even greater reward.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Devotion to מילה according to רבי אליעזר's ruling brought the city long life and protection from the decree against מילה.

steps.title: A מצוה accepted with joy is still done with joy
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that מצוות Israel accepted joyfully, like מילה, are still performed joyfully.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, every מצוה that the Jews accepted on themselves with joy, like מילה, is still done with joy. We see the joy from the פסוק: 'I rejoice over Your word like one who finds great treasure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that continues the theme of how special מילה is to the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the way a מצוה was first accepted shapes how it is kept for all generations. The proof that מילה was accepted with joy is the פסוק 'שש אנכי על אמרתך'. 'Your word' is read as referring to מילה. That is why a ברית is still a happy celebration today.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Every מצוה that they accepted upon themselves with joy,
such as circumcision, as it is written:
"I rejoice over Your word
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:162. 'Your word' is understood as the מצוה of מילה.

phrases.english: like one who finds great spoils"
they still perform it with joy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of Israel's devotion to מילה that began with the city that followed רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצוה accepted with joy, like מילה, continues to be performed with joy.

steps.title: A מצוה accepted with complaint still brings conflict
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the same ברייתא: מצוות accepted with complaint, like עריות, still bring arguments, which is why every כתובה involves a fight.
steps.simpleTranslation: And every מצוה that they accepted with complaint, like the laws of forbidden relationships, is still done with conflict. We see the complaint from the פסוק 'משה heard the people crying for their families.' This means they cried about family matters. That is why there is no כתובה that does not involve some argument.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל finishes his teaching with the opposite case: a מצוה the people received unhappily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'בוכה למשפחותיו' is read as 'crying over family matters'. The people cried because relatives they used to be allowed to marry became forbidden. Since עריות were accepted with tears, marriage arrangements still come with tension. Every כתובה ends up with some dispute.
steps.confusionAlert: 'למשפחותיו' plainly means 'family by family'. Here חז"ל read it as 'about family matters', meaning the newly forbidden relatives. Do not mix up the simple meaning with the דרשה.
steps.whatToRemember: How a מצוה was first received (with joy or with complaint) sets the tone for how it is kept in every generation.

phrases.english: And every מצוה that they accepted upon themselves with quarreling,
such as forbidden relations, as it is written:
"And Moses heard the people
weeping for their families"
meaning, over matters of their families,
they still perform it with quarreling,
for there is no marriage contract
in which they do not cast a quarrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting half of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצוה accepted with complaint, like עריות, continues to involve conflict, as seen in every כתובה.

steps.title: מצוות Israel gave their lives for are held firmly
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that מצוות the Jews sacrificed their lives for during the government's decrees, like עבודה זרה and מילה, are still kept strongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says, every מצוה that the Jews gave their lives for when the government made decrees against it, like avoiding עבודה זרה and doing מילה, is still held firmly in their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with another way of explaining why מילה is kept so strongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reason is not joy but self-sacrifice. Because Jews were ready to die rather than give up מילה and rather than serve idols, these מצוות became deeply rooted. They are still kept carefully.

keyTerms.meaning: They gave themselves over to death, meaning they risked their lives
Held firmly in their hands, kept strongly

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Every מצוה for which Israel gave themselves over
to death
at the time of the government's decree,
such as idolatry and circumcision,
it is still held firmly in their hands,

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא praising מילה, this time based on self-sacrifice instead of joy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצוות for which Israel risked their lives under persecution, like עבודה זרה and מילה, are still kept firmly.

steps.title: מצוות Israel did not give their lives for are kept loosely
steps.stepSummary: The other half of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's teaching: תפילין, which the Jews did not die for, are kept weakly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And every מצוה that the Jews did not give their lives for at the time of the government's decree, like תפילין, is still kept loosely and weakly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives the contrasting case: a מצוה that people did not risk their lives for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין is the example of a מצוה that most people gave up under persecution. As a result, it never became as firmly rooted, and people are lax about it. This sets up the next step, which shows how hard proper תפילין observance is.

keyTerms.meaning: Loose or weak in their hands, kept carelessly

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִצְוָה שֶׁלֹּא מָסְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָן
phrases.english: And every מצוה for which Israel did not give themselves over
to death
at the time of the government's decree,
such as phylacteries,
it is still weak in their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִצְוָה שֶׁלֹּא מָסְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָן עָלֶיהָ לְמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's contrast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצוות not defended with self-sacrifice, like תפילין, remain weakly observed.

steps.title: תפילין require a clean body, like אלישע בעל כנפים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי's statement is brought to support the idea about תפילין: they need a clean body, as אלישע בעל כנפים had.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי ינאי said: תפילין require a clean body, like אלישע בעל כנפים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי ינאי's statement to back up what was just said about תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דאמר' ('as he said') ties this statement to the previous claim. There are two connections. First, תפילין are demanding (they need a clean body), so people became lax. Second, the example given is אלישע. His story, told below, shows that only an exceptional individual risked his life for תפילין, while the people in general did not.

keyTerms.meaning: אלישע, 'Man of Wings', a pious man known for a miracle

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yannai said:
Phylacteries require a clean body
like Elisha, Man of Wings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim that תפילין were not kept with self-sacrifice by Israel as a whole.
steps.raayaObject: That תפילין are a demanding מצוה which the people did not uphold with self-sacrifice, apart from exceptional individuals.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ינאי's statement that תפילין need a clean body like אלישע בעל כנפים.

steps.title: What does a clean body mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly 'a clean body' means for תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this 'clean body'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the definition of the term 'clean body' and sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי did not explain what makes a body 'clean'. The גמרא asks for the exact practical requirement.

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: Asking what the requirement of a 'clean body' means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term used in רבי ינאי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical meaning of 'גוף נקי' for wearing תפילין.

steps.title: אביי: no passing wind; רבא: no sleeping
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a clean body means not passing wind while wearing תפילין. רבא says it means not sleeping in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it means one should not pass wind while wearing them. רבא said: it means one should not sleep in them.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different definitions of what a clean body means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the concern is bodily cleanliness. One must be able to control oneself and not pass wind while wearing תפילין. According to רבא, the concern is sleeping in תפילין, since a person may become unclean or careless while asleep.

phrases.english: Abaye said: That he not pass wind in them,
Rava said: That he not sleep in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about what 'clean body' means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי: not passing wind in תפילין. רבא: not sleeping in תפילין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה for anyone wearing תפילין.

steps.title: Why was he called אלישע בעל כנפים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the nickname 'בעל כנפים' came from.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they call him 'אלישע בעל כנפים'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the strange nickname and sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having mentioned אלישע as the model of a clean body, the גמרא now explains the source of his name. The answer will show his self-sacrifice for תפילין.

phrases.english: And why did they call him
"Elisha, Man of Wings"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי קָרוּ לֵיהּ אֱלִישָׁע בַּעַל כְּנָפַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the הלכה back to the person mentioned in רבי ינאי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The origin of the name 'בעל כנפים'.

steps.title: The decree against תפילין and אלישע's defiance
steps.stepSummary: The wicked government decreed death for anyone wearing תפילין. אלישע wore them anyway in the marketplace, and an official saw him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the wicked government made a decree against the Jews: whoever puts תפילין on his head will have his brain pierced. But אלישע would put on תפילין and go out to the marketplace. One official saw him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the story that answers the question about the nickname.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact situation רבי שמעון בן אלעזר described: a government decree against a מצוה. Most Jews did not risk their lives for תפילין, but אלישע did, openly in public. Now an enforcer has spotted him.

phrases.english: For once the wicked kingdom decreed
a decree upon Israel
that anyone who puts phylacteries on his head
they will pierce his brain,
and Elisha would put on phylacteries
and went out to the marketplace,
and an official saw him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁפַּעַם אַחַת גָּזְרָה מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה גְּזֵרָה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering why he was called בעל כנפים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The story begins: אלישע defied the government's death decree against תפילין.

steps.title: The chase and the official's question
steps.stepSummary: אלישע ran and the official chased him. When caught, אלישע took off the תפילין and held them in his hand, and said they were dove's wings.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלישע ran away from him, and the official ran after him. When the official reached him, אלישע took the תפילין off his head and held them in his hand. The official said to him: 'What is in your hand?' He answered: 'Dove's wings.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues to its moment of danger: אלישע is caught holding the forbidden תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע did not throw the תפילין away to save himself. He held on to them. His answer, 'dove's wings', sets up the miracle that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He took them off his head

phrases.english: He ran from before him, and he ran after him.
Once he reached him,
he removed them from his head and held them in his hand.
He said to him: What is in your hand?
He said to him: Wings of a dove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אלישע was caught holding the תפילין and claimed they were dove's wings.

steps.title: The miracle and the source of the name
steps.stepSummary: When אלישע opened his hand, dove's wings were found in it. That is why he was called בעל כנפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He opened his hand, and dove's wings were found in it. Therefore they would call him 'בעל כנפים' (Man of Wings).
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a miracle, and the גמרא concludes by explaining the nickname.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A miracle turned the תפילין into dove's wings, saving אלישע. This answers the question of step 31. It also shows that one man's self-sacrifice for תפילין was rewarded, in contrast to the people as a whole, who did not risk their lives for this מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: מילה and avoiding עבודה זרה are kept firmly because Jews gave their lives for them. תפילין is kept loosely because only rare individuals, like אלישע בעל כנפים, risked their lives for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The dove is a symbol of Israel. Just as a dove protects itself with its wings, Israel is protected by its מצוות. This is a fitting image for the miracle.

phrases.english: He opened his hand
and wings of a dove were found in it.
Therefore they would call him
"Man of Wings."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ הָיוּ קוֹרְאִין אוֹתוֹ בַּעַל כְּנָפַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and answers the question of step 31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A miracle turned אלישע's תפילין into dove's wings, so he was called בעל כנפים. He stands as the rare example of self-sacrifice for תפילין.

steps.title: Why specifically a dove's wings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אלישע said the תפילין were dove's wings and not the wings of some other bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about a dove's wings, that he told the official that, and did not name the wings of some other bird?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the story we just finished. Why did אלישע name a dove, of all birds?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any bird's wings could have served as a cover story. So the גמרא assumes there must be a meaning behind choosing the יונה, and it asks what that meaning is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different / what is special about

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא כַּנְפֵי יוֹנָה דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: What is different about a dove's wings, that he told him that,
and he did not tell him the wings of other birds?
phrases.notes: 'He' is אלישע; 'him' is the official who caught him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא כַּנְפֵי יוֹנָה דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail in the story concluded in step 34: why אלישע chose the dove.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason אלישע named dove's wings specifically, rather than any other bird.

steps.title: The Jewish people are like a dove protected by its wings
steps.stepSummary: כנסת ישראל is compared to a יונה in תהלים. A dove is protected by its wings, and the Jewish people are protected by their מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because כנסת ישראל is compared to a dove, as the פסוק says: 'the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with shining gold.' Just as a dove's wings protect it, so too the Jewish people's מצוות protect them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. אלישע said 'dove's wings' because the dove stands for the Jewish people, and wings stand for מצוות that protect them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from a פסוק in תהלים (68:14) that describes Israel as a dove. The comparison is this: a dove's wings protect it, and מצוות protect the Jewish people. This fits the story well, because the תפילין, a מצוה, turned into wings that protected אלישע from the official.

keyTerms.meaning: The community of Israel, the Jewish people as a whole

steps.whatToRemember: The dove (יונה) is a symbol of the Jewish people. Its wings are like מצוות: they are what protect us. In the story, the תפילין literally became the wings that saved אלישע.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the miracle into a message. Keeping a מצוה even at great risk, as אלישע did, is exactly what protects the Jewish people.

phrases.english: Because the community of Israel is compared to a dove,
as it is said: 'The wings of a dove covered with silver,'
'and her feathers with shining gold.'

phrases.aramaic: מַה יּוֹנָה זוֹ כְּנָפֶיהָ מְגִינּוֹת עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: Just as this dove, its wings protect it,
so too Israel, מצוות protect them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35 and closes the אלישע בעל כנפים story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dove symbolizes כנסת ישראל (תהלים 68:14). Its wings protect it the way מצוות protect the Jewish people.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מצוות are the protective 'wings' of the Jewish people.

steps.title: The story of the forgotten scalpel for a ברית on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר רב אדא quotes רבי יצחק: once people forgot to bring the איזמל before שבת. They brought it on שבת by way of roofs and courtyards. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר רב אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: One time they forgot and did not bring the scalpel before שבת, so they brought it on שבת by way of roofs and courtyards...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story connected to מילה on שבת. It is still being set up here, and its point will come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying a tool on שבת is normally forbidden. Our פרק discusses whether the needs of a ברית מילה allow bringing the knife on שבת. The route matters: roofs and courtyards are not a public street (רשות הרבים). Why they took this route, and whether it was allowed, is discussed on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A scalpel / knife used for מילה

steps.confusionAlert: The story is not finished here. Don't draw a conclusion yet about what רבי יצחק is proving; the גמרא continues the story on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר רַב אַדָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Rav Adda said
that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
One time they forgot
and did not bring a scalpel before Shabbat,
and they brought it on Shabbat
by way of roofs and by way of courtyards,
phrases.notes: They avoided the public street. The story continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the אלישע אגדה to a new story about bringing the מילה knife on שבת, the main topic of the פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story is being set up: the איזמל was forgotten before שבת and was brought on שבת via roofs and courtyards. Its lesson comes on the next amud.
